methods: solving a trigonometric equation with range restrictions
statement: Show that $\\sin3\\theta+\\sin\\theta=2\\sin2\\theta\\cos\\theta$. Hence solve the equation $\\sin3\\theta+\\sin\\theta=\\sin2\\theta$ for $0\\le\\theta<2\\pi$, giving all solutions.
solution: Using $\\sin A+\\sin B=2\\sin\\tfrac{A+B}{2}\\cos\\tfrac{A-B}{2}$, we get $\\sin3\\theta+\\sin\\theta=2\\sin2\\theta\\cos\\theta$. The equation becomes $2\\sin2\\theta\\cos\\theta=\\sin2\\theta$, so $\\sin2\\theta(2\\cos\\theta-1)=0$. Either $\\sin2\\theta=0$, giving $2\\theta=k\\pi$ so $\\theta=0,\\tfrac{\\pi}{2},\\pi,\\tfrac{3\\pi}{2}$; or $2\\cos\\theta-1=0$, i.e. $\\cos\\theta=\\tfrac12$, giving $\\theta=\\tfrac{\\pi}{3},\\tfrac{5\\pi}{3}$. The full solution set is $\\theta=0,\\tfrac{\\pi}{3},\\tfrac{\\pi}{2},\\pi,\\tfrac{3\\pi}{2},\\tfrac{5\\pi}{3}$.
hints: Use the sum-to-product identity to combine sin3θ and sinθ.
Factor out sin2θ to split the equation.
Solve sin2θ = 0 and cosθ = 1/2 separately, collecting all θ in [0,2π).
